company_verdict: Fractal is absolutely worth his time — it is the single best brand-to-profile match in Indian analytics for a DJSCE data-science student with a case-competition record — but almost none of that value sits on the careers portal. Of 136 live reqs globally and 67 in India, ZERO are internships, trainee, graduate or campus positions; the four whose written qualification blocks contain no years bar at all are still full-time billable delivery seats, three of which expire 30 Nov 2026, and none of them will hold a seat open for a June-2027 joiner. The real door is the referral-only "Imagineers" Data & AI Trainee programme: the 2026 drive took 2026 pass-outs only, demanded 7.0 CGPA throughout, circuit branches only, employee-referral submission only, with a three-day window in late January — his 8.82 CGPA, B.Tech CSE (Data Science) at DJSCE and Mumbai base clear that bar comfortably. The work to do in the next 90 days is therefore not applying; it is manufacturing a warm Fractal contact before December 2026, because when the 2027 window opens there will be no public apply link.
best_channel: REFERRAL-ONLY GRADUATE PROGRAMME — Fractal "Imagineers (Data & AI Trainee)", 2027-batch intake. Justification: it is the only Fractal pipeline that (a) is designed for a fresh graduating batch rather than an experienced hire, (b) has a published eligibility bar he clears on every line (B.E/B.Tech circuit branch — CSE counts; minimum 7 CGPA throughout vs his 8.82; no active backlogs), (c) lists Mumbai as a joining location, and (d) runs four tracks — Data Science, Data Engineering, Decision Sciences, Data Visualisation — three of which map to what he actually wants (analytics/BI/decision science, not SDE). The 2026 drive opened 28 Jan 2026 and closed 30 Jan 2026 with submission by employee referral only, announced through WhatsApp/Telegram off-campus channels. If the pattern repeats, the 2027-batch window is Dec 2026 – Feb 2027. SECONDARY CHANNEL: a Jan–May 2027 final-semester internship (Fractal has run Mumbai summer internships in past cycles and a Bengaluru Growth Analytics internship is currently listed on an aggregator with a PPO attached) — this is the only format that can actually employ him before June 2027. TERTIARY, near-worthless alone: the "Introduce Yourself" talent-community form at https://fractal.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/Careers — ten minutes, puts him in the Workday CRM recruiters search when a campus req is raised, but it is a black hole without a referral behind it. NOT a viable channel: ordinary experienced-hire reqs. Every single one is 3+ years, immediate-joiner, or expiring within ten weeks.
may_2027_fit: Fractal's portal is structurally closed to a May-2027 graduate and he should stop treating it as the main event. Concrete evidence: SR-45548 (Senior Snowflake Developer) opens with "Note - Immediate to 30 Days only"; SR-45903, SR-20652, SR-16018 and SR-38467 carry hard END DATES of 30 Nov / 31 Dec 2026; SR-46203 was posted today and closes tomorrow. None of these reqs can absorb a candidate whose earliest full-time start is June 2027 — eight months out. Conversely, the Imagineers programme is defined by batch year: the 2026 drive said "2026 Pass-outs ONLY", which means the 2027 drive will say 2027 pass-outs only and he will be exactly the target, not a stretch — the same profile that is unhireable on the portal today is the default hire there. Two dates should go in his calendar now: 15 Dec 2026 (start pinging every Fractal contact weekly for the Imagineers referral link — the window is three days and there is no public URL) and 1 Nov 2026 (start applying to Jan–May 2027 final-semester internships, Fractal-linked and otherwise). Start dates he should state in writing: for any internship — "5 January 2027 to 30 May 2027, full-time, on-site"; for any full-time req or Imagineers form — "graduating May 2027, available to join from 1 June 2027" (say June, not July; it reads as eager and still leaves buffer). He should never hide the 2027 date to get past a screen; at Fractal the date is not a liability in the channel that matters, it is the eligibility criterion.

picks.title: Data Scientist - Gen AI
picks.location: Bengaluru (primary); also open in MUMBAI, Pune, Chennai, Hyderabad, Gurgaon, Noida
picks.years_bar: None stated anywhere in the posting, and the grade is plain "Data Scientist" with no seniority prefix. This is the lowest written bar of any live Fractal India req.
picks.why_fit: Posted: "Proficiency with SaaS LLMs, including Lang chain, llama index, vector databases, Prompt engineering (COT, TOT, ReAct, agents)" → KOP AI orchestrates 10 stateful LLM agents in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor with RAG over PDFs and YouTube returning page-and-timestamp citations on ChromaDB — that is a vector database, agent orchestration and prompt engineering in one shipped project, with a measurable 60-90s → 8-12s (~7x) latency result. Posted: "Application Development: Proficiency in Python, Docker, FastAPI/Django/Flask, and Git" → exactly LawzyAI (FastAPI, scikit-learn, React, live site) and KOP AI (Next.js, FastAPI, ChromaDB, Groq, Llama 3.1); Docker and Git are both on his skills list. Posted: "Natural Language Processing: use case classification, topic modeling, Q&A and chatbots, search, Document AI, summarization" → LawzyAI maps plain-language narratives to IPC and BNS sections via LLM query normalisation feeding TF-IDF retrieval, which is classification plus search plus Document AI on legal text; CypherSOL's transaction-category and entity-recognition models replacing rule-based analytics is production-adjacent NLP on financial documents. Critically, this req writes the primary skill as an explicit AND/OR — "NLP ... AND/OR Computer Vision and Audio" — so LearnSphere (ONNX FER+ emotion engine, OpenCV, per-user SVM correcting domain bias) satisfies the second branch independently. He clears the primary skill from both directions. Education demanded is B.E/B.Tech in CS or equivalent, which is exactly what he will hold.
picks.gaps: Named vendor platforms he has never touched: "Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock" — he has used Groq and Llama 3.1, none of the three named. "Lang chain, llama index" are named verbatim and he built KOP AI's orchestration by hand with ThreadPoolExecutor, not in either framework. "TensorFlow/Pytorch and huggingface" — he has scikit-learn and ONNX Runtime, none of these three. "quantization, LLM finetuning using PEFT, RLHF, data annotation workflow, and GPU utilization" — nothing on his resume touches any of these five; this is the single weakest line for him. "Cloud certification is preferred" — an AWS Academy Machine Learning Foundations badge is a course completion, not a cloud certification. And the unwritten blocker that actually decides this: it is a billable delivery seat with no intern grade, so his June-2027 availability, not his skills, is what gets him screened out.
picks.learnable_edge: Four items, all genuinely 2-6 weeks and each tied to a named bullet. (1) Port KOP AI's retrieval layer to LlamaIndex and its agent loop to LangChain/LangGraph — 2 weekends — this turns the two verbatim-named framework gaps into a public repo link, and it is a refactor of code he already wrote, not a new project. (2) Run one existing pipeline through AWS Bedrock using his existing AWS account — 1 weekend — satisfies "AWS Bedrock" literally. (3) A LoRA/PEFT fine-tune of a small model on HuggingFace for the CypherSOL-style transaction-category task — 2 weekends on a free Colab T4 — hits "huggingface", "LLM finetuning using PEFT" and "GPU utilization" in one artefact. (4) AZ-900 or AWS Cloud Practitioner — 2-3 weeks — satisfies "Cloud certification is preferred" as written. Note there is no Java, C++, Scala or Spark anywhere in this posting.
picks.referral_leverage: high — this is THE req to hand a referrer, because the written bar contains no years number and no degree he lacks, so a referrer is arguing for the candidate rather than against the JD. Target a Fractal Data Scientist or Senior Data Scientist who is a DJSCE alumnus (LinkedIn: company Fractal + school Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering, filter Mumbai and Bengaluru). Ask them to submit the internal referral with one specific line in the notes field: "2027 graduate, available Jan-May 2027 as a full-time intern and from June 2027 full-time." That notes field is the ONLY place in the Workday flow where his timeline can be stated before the ATS bins him — and the same referrer becomes his Imagineers link in December.
picks.timing: Realistically no for the seat itself; yes for the relationship. The req has no end date and no stated start date, so it will be filled long before June 2027. He should still apply, because the purpose is to get a recruiter conversation and a CRM record tagged before the 2027 Imagineers intake, not to win this seat. Declared availability: "Available Jan-May 2027 as a final-semester intern; full-time from 1 June 2027."

picks.title: Senior Engineer — posting body titles it "Hacker-Mind AI Engineer"
picks.location: Bengaluru (primary); also open in MUMBAI, Pune, Chennai, Gurgaon. Body says "Location: Bangalore, Mumbai".
picks.years_bar: "5+ years of experience in software/data/AI engineering (or equivalent open-source/portfolio proof)" — the only experience clause at Fractal India that is written as satisfiable WITHOUT years.

KOP AI (10 stateful LLM agents orchestrated in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor, 60-90s → 8-12s, ~7x faster), LawzyAI (live site plus GitHub), and GitLane (custom HTTP/1.1 server over raw TCP sockets, Git packfile protocol, write-ahead push queue, offline-first) are portfolio proof of a genuinely unusual kind — GitLane in particular is systems-level work that most 5-year analytics hires could not produce. Posted: "Fluency in Python and at least one systems or compiled language (e.g., Rust, Go, TypeScript)" → TypeScript is on his resume and is the listed escape hatch, so this clause is satisfiable without touching Rust, Go, Java or C++. Posted Bonus Points: "Open-source contributions or personal GitHub projects" → github.com/Meanwhile-omkar; "Experience working with or building LLM-powered systems" → KOP AI and LawzyAI; "Participation in hackathons, AI challenges, or research communities" → 13 podium finishes, Winner of Analytrix'26 Datathon and ML Quest Hackathon, Top 1000 globally on Unstop. Posted: "Ability to work across the stack: data wrangling, modeling, API design" → CypherSOL (multi-format bank-statement cleaning into model-ready data, then category and entity-recognition models) plus FastAPI services across two projects. Posted: "comfortable being the technical lead in an ambiguous environment ... you're a problem definer" → Infiheal founder's-office work, where he owned Series A materials end-to-end and drove IndiGo and HDFC Bank from first contact to proposal.
picks.gaps: Be honest about four things. (1) "Hands-on experience with AI/ML frameworks: PyTorch, TensorFlow, HuggingFace, LangChain" — he has literally none of the four named frameworks; scikit-learn and ONNX Runtime are not on this list. (2) "containers, orchestration, CI/CD, IaC (Docker, K8s, Terraform)" — Docker only. No Kubernetes, no Terraform, no CI/CD pipeline he has owned. (3) "MLOps" is in the across-the-stack line and is absent from his resume entirely. (4) It is a SENIOR ENGINEER grade — the portfolio clause lowers the years bar, it does not lower the grade, and he would be competing against people who have shipped production systems in a team. And the strategic objection: this is the most engineering-heavy role on his list and it sits against his stated preference to avoid core software engineering. Only pursue it if he would genuinely accept an AI-prototyping engineer seat.
picks.learnable_edge: (1) LangChain/LangGraph plus HuggingFace transformers — 2-3 weekends, by porting KOP AI — closes half of the framework bullet without any new project. (2) One GitHub Actions CI pipeline plus a docker-compose → kind/minikube deployment of LawzyAI — 1-2 weekends — converts "containers, orchestration, CI/CD" from zero to demonstrable with a public workflow file as evidence. (3) Terraform basics — 1 weekend — provision one small AWS stack (S3 + EC2 + IAM) from a .tf file and commit it; that is enough to speak to IaC credibly. Explicitly NOT needed: Rust or Go — TypeScript on his resume already satisfies the clause, and he should say so in the first line of his note.
picks.referral_leverage: medium-high — the posting names the team ("Data & AI Innovation"), which is rare and means a referrer can route him to a specific hiring manager rather than into the general Workday pool. But the referrer is arguing against a Senior grade, not against a years bar, which is a harder conversation than SR-42761. Best used as a second referral, not a first.
picks.timing: Posted with a start date of June 2025 and still open with no end date — this is an evergreen innovation-team req, which makes it the ONE experienced-hire posting here plausibly still alive in 2027. Strategy: apply now to establish the record, then re-check it in January 2027 and re-apply if it is still live. Declare "available from 1 June 2027; open to Jan-May 2027 as a full-time intern on the innovation team's R&D sprints" — an R&D team is the most likely place at Fractal to say yes to an intern.

skills_to_learn.skill: LangChain (+ LangGraph) and LlamaIndex — by porting KOP AI's existing retrieval and agent layer into them
skills_to_learn.why: Named verbatim as "Lang chain, llama index" in the mandatory skills of FIVE live reqs: SR-42761, SR-20652, SR-45903, SR-43796, and (as "LangChain") SR-32787. It is the single most-repeated named gap between his resume and Fractal's India postings. He already built the hard part — 10 stateful agents orchestrated in parallel with RAG and citation-accurate retrieval — by hand with ThreadPoolExecutor; expressing it in the two frameworks Fractal names is a refactor, not a new project, and it produces a public repo link that answers the bullet literally. It is also mandatory preparation for SR-43796, whose posting states GenAI skills "will be evaluated during the interviews".
skills_to_learn.effort: 2 weekends to a credible level (port the retrieval layer to LlamaIndex, the agent loop to LangGraph); a third weekend if he also writes a short README comparing his hand-rolled orchestration's latency to the framework version — that comparison is an interview story no bootcamp graduate has.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: LangChain and LlamaIndex official quickstart docs, plus DeepLearning.AI's free short courses "LangChain for LLM Application Development" and "Building Agentic RAG with LlamaIndex". Zero cost, runs on his existing Groq free tier.

skills_to_learn.skill: PyTorch + HuggingFace transformers, including one LoRA/PEFT fine-tune
skills_to_learn.why: "TensorFlow/Pytorch and huggingface" plus "quantization, LLM finetuning using PEFT, RLHF" appear in SR-42761, SR-20652, SR-45903 and SR-43796; "PyTorch, TensorFlow, HuggingFace" in SR-32787; "Expertise in PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Keras" in SR-44870 (Computer Vision); "NLTK, SpaCy, or TensorFlow" and "deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow or PyTorch" in SR-45838 and SR-45840. That is up to eight reqs touching one gap. He currently has scikit-learn and ONNX Runtime — neither is named in any Fractal posting. The highest-value version is not a tutorial: LoRA fine-tune a small model on the CypherSOL-style transaction-category task, which simultaneously satisfies "huggingface", "LLM finetuning using PEFT" and "GPU utilization" while retelling real internship work.
skills_to_learn.effort: 2-3 weekends. Weekend 1: HuggingFace pipelines and a Trainer loop on a public text-classification set. Weekend 2-3: the PEFT/LoRA fine-tune on his own transaction-category data, on a free Colab T4.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: HuggingFace NLP Course (chapters 1-3 and 7), the PEFT library quickstart, and Google Colab's free T4. No paid compute needed for a small model.

skills_to_learn.skill: One hyperscaler LLM service — AWS Bedrock (fastest given his AWS Academy account) or Azure OpenAI
skills_to_learn.why: "Experience with Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock for text/audio/image/video modalities" is a named bullet in FOUR reqs (SR-42761, SR-20652, SR-45903, SR-43796), and "Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS, and GCP" sits alongside it in the same four. He has shipped on Groq and Llama 3.1 — real LLM engineering, but zero of the three platforms Fractal names. Re-pointing one existing project's LLM calls at Bedrock converts a hard "no" into a literal "yes" on that bullet. Fractal's delivery work is heavily Azure-flavoured (see the P&G Azure reqs), so Azure OpenAI is the better long-term bet if he has student credits.

skills_to_learn.resource: Free/near-free: AWS Bedrock workshop (workshops.aws) on the free tier, or Microsoft Learn's "Develop Generative AI solutions with Azure OpenAI Service" path with Azure for Students credits (free with a college email — DJSCE qualifies).

skills_to_learn.skill: AZ-900 (Azure Fundamentals) or AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
skills_to_learn.why: "Cloud certification is preferred" is written inline in FOUR reqs (SR-42761, SR-20652, SR-45903, SR-43796), and "Foundational Knowledge of Cloud Computing either one AWS, Azure or GCP" is a required bullet in SR-16018. It is the only Fractal preference on this list that a two-to-three week effort converts from "preferred" to "held" with a verifiable credential ID — and his current AWS Academy Machine Learning Foundations badge is a course completion, not a certification, which a sharp recruiter will notice. AZ-900 is also the right signal for Fractal India specifically, given how much of their delivery stack (ADF, ADLS2, Databricks on Azure) is Microsoft.
skills_to_learn.effort: 2-3 weeks of evenings to pass. AZ-900 is the easier of the two and Microsoft frequently runs free Virtual Training Days that include a free exam voucher — worth waiting for rather than paying.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: Microsoft Learn's official AZ-900 learning path plus a Microsoft Virtual Training Day for the free voucher; or freeCodeCamp's full CLF-C02 course on YouTube (exam ~$100).

skills_to_learn.skill: A/B testing and experiment design + SQL window functions, evidenced on his own funnel data
skills_to_learn.why: "A/B Testing", "Product Analytics", "SQL" and "Advanced Excel" are four of the six stated skills on the Growth Analytics Intern listing — the highest-scoring posting on his entire shortlist and the only one with a Pre-Placement Offer attached. Experimentation is also the subject matter of SR-41535 (retail experimentation platform) and is core to the Imagineers Decision Sciences track, which is his most likely route in. He already owns the rarest ingredient: real funnel drop-off data from a 10,000-user registration platform he built, plus an automated WhatsApp/SMS re-engagement loop. Turning that into a written experiment readout is the difference between claiming A/B testing and evidencing it.
skills_to_learn.effort: 1-2 weekends total: one for experiment design fundamentals (hypothesis, sample size, power, guardrail metrics, novelty effect) and the readout, one for SQL window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LAG/LEAD, running totals, cohort retention queries) which he needs anyway for every analyst screen in India.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: Udacity's A/B Testing course (ud257), Mode Analytics SQL Tutorial (advanced section) and StrataScratch's free window-function problems. Zero cost.

skills_to_learn.why: Lower priority for the live reqs — only SR-39565 names it ("Proficient in Power BI, Tableau, Qlik, Looker, etc.", 10+ years, out of reach) — but it matters for the channel that actually hires him: the Imagineers programme runs a dedicated Data Visualisation track described as PowerBI/Tableau/custom UI. He already has Power BI, so Tableau is the cheapest possible second tool and it makes him eligible for two of the four Imagineers tracks instead of one. It is also the default BI tool ask across every other Indian analytics employer he will apply to, so the effort does not go to waste if Fractal does not convert.
skills_to_learn.effort: 2 weekends to a portfolio-credible level: rebuild one existing Power BI dashboard in Tableau Public (the Spotify EDA from the Datazen win is the obvious candidate — it is already a story he has won a competition with) and publish it to a public profile link.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: Tableau Public (free download and free hosting) plus Tableau's own free "Get Started" training videos. The published profile URL goes straight on his resume.

referral_strategy:
A referral is not a nice-to-have at Fractal — for his batch it is the entire mechanism, because the only pipeline he is actually eligible for accepts NO direct applications. Concretely, four moves, in this order.

(1) BUILD THE LIST NOW, NOT IN DECEMBER. LinkedIn people search: current company "Fractal" (also try "Fractal Analytics") + school "Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering", filtered to Mumbai and Bengaluru. Fractal hires heavily from Mumbai engineering colleges and its Mumbai office is a major delivery centre, so this list will not be empty. Target grade matters: a Data Scientist or Senior Data Scientist (2-5 years in) is the ideal referrer — junior enough to answer a student's message, senior enough that their referral is weighted, and crucially ANY employee at any grade can submit an Imagineers referral. Aim for six to eight warm contacts by 30 November 2026, not one.

(2) USE THE ASSETS HE ALREADY HAS THAT MOST STUDENTS DON'T. As Head of Marketing at DJS S4DS and Vice Chairperson of Trinity, he books judges and speakers — invite a Fractal data scientist to judge or speak at an S4DS event in Oct-Nov 2026. That inverts the dynamic completely: he is offering something, not asking, and a judge who has watched him run an event will submit a referral without hesitation. Second asset: Analytics Vidhya is Fractal-owned (see SR-46203, filed under Analytics Vidhya Educon inside the same Workday tenant) — he is an Analytrix'26 Datathon winner and an ML Quest Hackathon winner, so an AV DataHack leaderboard finish or a published AV blog post is a Fractal-adjacent credential that gets noticed internally. Third: his Infiheal founder's-office network reached investors, IndiGo and HDFC Bank — ask his Infiheal founder directly for a warm intro into Fractal; founders in the Mumbai AI ecosystem know Fractal people.

(3) MAKE TWO DISTINCT ASKS, NOT ONE. Ask A (now, low cost to the referrer): submit an internal referral on SR-42761 "Data Scientist - Gen AI" with one specific line in the notes field — "2027 graduate, available Jan-May 2027 as a full-time intern and from June 2027 full-time." That notes field is the only place in the Workday flow where his timeline can be stated before an ATS screens him out, and SR-42761 is the right req to spend it on because its written bar contains no years number and no degree he lacks. Ask B (the one that actually matters): "When the Imagineers 2027 referral window opens — the 2026 drive ran 28-30 January with a three-day window and no public apply link — will you send me the link the day it drops?" Then set a calendar reminder for 15 December 2026 and ping every contact weekly through February. A three-day window loses to a slow inbox; that is the whole risk.

(4) DO THE TEN-MINUTE PORTAL TASK THIS WEEK. "Introduce Yourself" at https://fractal.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/Careers puts his profile into the Workday CRM that Fractal recruiters search when a campus or trainee req is raised. On its own it is a black hole and he should expect nothing from it — but it costs ten minutes and it means that when a recruiter sources for the 2027 Imagineers intake, a DJSCE CSE-Data Science profile with 8.82 CGPA and a GenAI portfolio is already in the system. Pair it with a referral; never rely on it alone.

WHERE A REFERRAL DOES NOT HELP, and he should not waste one: SR-42100 / SR-43592 / SR-25671 (Azure Data Engineer, 6-9 and 6-10 years), SR-22272 (Data Modeler, 7-10), SR-38467 (Data Governance, 8-12), SR-40814 (RGM, 7+ and 10 overall), SR-39565 (Lead Architect BI, 10+), SR-40397 (Engagement Manager, 10+), SR-41535 (Senior Product Owner, 10-15), SR-42046 (Senior Data Scientist, 5.6-11), SR-45548 (Snowflake, "Immediate to 30 Days only"), SR-46203 (SME, 6+ and closes tomorrow), SR-45903 (title says 3-5 years). Also rule out SR-42992 Manager-Reporting and SR-44168 Manager-Commercial Finance: both are gated on a Chartered Accountant / CMA / CFA / MBA credential he does not hold and cannot acquire in weeks — the low "1-2 years" and "2-3 years" figures on those two are a trap that will surface in any naive low-experience scan. A referral moves a years bar by one or two years at most; it does not move eight, and it does not manufacture a CA.
